objective: Compose the checked weekly TCS6 selector with existing scheduled DCS2 event materialization, then establish accepted-only daily-counter ownership in the existing irrigation carrier.
first_phase: Pure explicit daily-selection composition: input dayfix and explicit daily invocation, output proposed dayfix plus existing event/flux/diagnostics. Reuse evaluate_tcs6_weekly_timing without changing its strict deficit threshold or increment/reset order. Extend typed scheduled timing validation only for this explicit criterion, preserving ordinary entry rejection. Pending gifts do not invoke a new selector. Do not publish the proposed counter in the process layer.
gates: Source startup dayfix=366 and seventh-day reset with both triggering and nontriggering deficit.
Counter reset occurs on the seventh daily invocation even if no gift is selected; a no-gift day is not a no-state-change day.
Retried and split-required trials always derive from the same committed counter and never increment it twice.
All source counter/deficit/threshold invalid-input guards; ordinary entry stays fail-closed; TCS1-4 and TCS7/8 preservation.

Before runtime integration, specify daily invocation identity and its persistence with the counter inside the sole existing committed carrier, including inactive/no-gift states, decoded restart, duplicate daily requests, all-column preflight and mixed hydraulic publication.
ownership_constraints: No module SAVE counter, calendar singleton, second state owner, or caller-side mutable counter publication. Process outputs are proposals only. Runtime must publish counter and event/hydraulics atomically per accepted column; failed trials retain all committed fields. A source-only passing test cannot qualify daily runtime ownership.
non_goals: File/date parsing, implicit day detection, automatic crop rotation, surface delivery, solute transport, changing numerical acceptance or canonical admission. DCS1 extension follows separately after DCS2 lifecycle qualification.
